projects.summary: The project will transform Ellesmere Port Market Hall into a more attractive destination, demolish empty buildings at Civic Offices and Coronation Road to free land for new homes, and create a safe cycle route from the train station to the market.
projects.justification: Construction verifiably underway: market Phase One completed January 2026, active travel works starting January 2026, Civic Way demolition completed July 2025.

citations.finding: Work began March 2025 on market transformation, active travel routes, and housing site assembly with solar panels installed.
Market refurbishment Phase One completed January 2026, entire market expected to reopen late summer 2026.
Active travel route works scheduled with road closures from January to April 2026, market completion autumn 2026.
Former council offices on Civic Way demolished by July 2025 to make way for new housing.

projects.summary: The Workington Gateway project will deliver junction enhancements where the A66 and A596 intersect at Ramsey Brow, improvements to pedestrian and cycling facilities in the town centre, and upgrades to Workington Hall including feature lighting and a new Social Enterprise Centre within the Walled Garden.
projects.justification: Demolition began August 2024, construction underway, but explicitly delayed with completion extended to June 2026 due to engineering challenges.

citations.finding: Demolition work started 7 August 2024 to enable the project.
Scheme extended to 11 April 2026 completion due to engineering challenges during construction.
Phase 1 unfortunately delayed, now expected completion June 2026.
Phase two of scheme began 23 February 2026, work continuing.

projects.summary: The Barrow-in-Furness Town Centre project is a £17.5 million Levelling Up Fund scheme to reinvigorate the Market Hall, neighbouring arts and entertainment venue The Forum, and the surrounding public realm to attract more people into the town centre and boost the local economy.
projects.justification: Original Market Hall refurbishment plans formally cancelled June 2025; scope changed to demolition and broader transformation.

citations.finding: Cabinet agreed June 3 to not progress current plans for Market Hall refurbishment, favour bolder vision.
Plans to refurbish market hall with £23.5m budget will now not go ahead.
Council agreed to start process for bolder plans; original £17.5m LUF secured 2021.
Demolition works at Dalton Road/Stephen Street/Ginnel started November 2023, completion early 2024.

projects.summary: The Industrial Solutions Hub (iSH) Enterprise Campus in Cleator Moor involves constructing 1,683 sq m of academic/R&D space, an interim Meanwhile Hub, and an active travel route connecting the town centre to the campus, aiming to deliver economic regeneration and job creation focused on robotics, manufacturing, and digital sectors.
projects.justification: First industrial units became available August 2025; additional units approved April 2026 for summer 2027 delivery.

citations.finding: First two units (Unit 9 and Unit 12) released on August 20, 2025.
First industrial units available at campus as of August 14, 2025.
Plans approved April 15, 2026 for two additional industrial buildings at the campus.
Two new buildings approved, expected available summer 2027, part of ongoing campus development.

projects.summary: The Energy Coast Resilient Routes project will upgrade 30km of Cumbria's highway network to improve journey reliability and safety, reduce road closures due to highway defects, and better connect communities to jobs and services across the county.
projects.justification: Construction works commenced January 2024 on A5086 and A595; resurfacing reached 200,000m2 by late 2024.

citations.finding: Works commenced Monday 8 January 2024 on A5086 between Rowrah and Crossgates.
Story Contracting appointed as lead contractor with works planned to start Autumn 2024.
Resurfacing works reached 200,000m2 on A5086 and A595 routes.
A5086 and A595 upgrades underway as part of £14.3m infrastructure improvement.

projects.summary: The Bolton College of Medical Sciences is a £30m project receiving £20m from the Levelling Up Fund to build a new facility in Farnworth, delivered through a partnership between the University of Bolton, Bolton Council, Bolton NHS Foundation Trust, and Bolton College to transform NHS staff training by enabling students to train on the hospital site.
projects.justification: Building construction completed May 2024; facility opened for student applications and courses began September 2024.

citations.finding: Building work completed May 2024, with internal fit-out underway ahead of September opening.
Institute of Medical Sciences opened for applications in September 2024.
Bolton Institute of Medical Sciences marked completion of its state-of-the-art facilities.
First MBChB Medicine students welcomed into the new £40m Institute of Medical Sciences.

projects.summary: The Radcliffe Civic and Enterprise Hub Development will create a new facility in Radcliffe town centre featuring a leisure centre with pool and climbing facilities, relocated library, refurbished market spaces, and offices, aiming to establish a focus for leisure, learning, community, and enterprise.
projects.justification: Construction actively underway with swimming pool installation and cladding work, but completion extended from winter 2024 to July 2026.

citations.finding: Hub currently being constructed with cladding work scheduled September to November 2025.
Swimming pool installation milestone reached; completion expected winter 2025/26 to spring 2026.
Council expected work complete by winter 2024 when construction began in 2023.
Completion date confirmed as July 6, 2026, approximately 18 months later than original target.

projects.summary: The project will deliver essential improvements to Bury Market, voted Britain's favourite market in 2019, and construct a new flexible venue (flexi hall) to serve as a focus for leisure, events, and enterprise within enhanced public realm.
projects.justification: Construction verifiably underway: groundbreaking January 2025, steel erection April 2025, foundation and frame works progressing September 2025, no adverse news.

citations.finding: Groundbreaking ceremony held 21 January 2025 marking start of building work for Flexi Hall.
Structural steelwork being erected outside trading hours as of April 2025.
Foundation and steel frame works well underway by September 2025, concrete poured, timber frame being built.
Official council page confirms construction of Flexi Hall is underway with completion expected mid-2026.

projects.project_name: The Culture in the City project
projects.summary: The Culture in the City project will regenerate the Upper and Lower Campfield buildings and market area to deliver high-quality, affordable workspace for the tech and creative sectors in Manchester city centre.
projects.justification: Campfield campus officially opened June 25, 2025, after £17.5m transformation of Upper Campfield Market into creative tech hub.

citations.finding: Campfield officially opened its doors on June 25, 2025 in Manchester's St John's neighbourhood.
Historic Manchester landmark reborn as Campfield, a £17.5m creative hub blending co-working, culture, and community.
Campfield reopened by Allied London in June as 130,000 sq ft creative tech development.
Culture In The City initiative received £17.5m Levelling Up funding for the project.

projects.summary: The Green Technology and Innovation Network project will create 2,285 square metres of incubation space for green businesses at the Green Shoots Centre, develop a pedestrian and cycling greenway linking key sites through the town centre including the new Jubilee Park, aiming to position Oldham as a sustainable destination for green businesses.
projects.justification: Construction underway on Northern Roots Visitor Centre, a key component; opening scheduled for summer/autumn 2026.

citations.finding: Oldham Council set to begin construction on £12.9m Visitor Centre at Northern Roots, part of Green Technology Innovation Network.
Construction work underway on visitors centre at Northern Roots, completion set for summer 2026.
Northern Roots Welcome Building construction ongoing, doors to open autumn 2026.
Green Shoots Centre supported by £9m Levelling Up Fund grant as part of Green Innovation programme.

projects.summary: The Salford Rise project will deliver major infrastructure improvements to connect local communities to the Crescent Innovation Zone, including enhanced public realm and connectivity works designed to attract over £90 million of investment into the area.
projects.justification: Construction began October 2024; piling works underway as of January 2025; bridge construction progressing toward summer 2026 completion.

citations.finding: Construction started October 2024 with Eric Wright Civil Engineering as main contractor.
Construction began January 2025; piling works 4.5m down and ground floor upgrades underway.
Preparatory works resumed February 3, 2025 with Frederick Road closure for construction.
May 2026 update shows bridge beam installation and balustrade work scheduled for completion.

projects.summary: The Ashton Town Centre Regeneration project, funded by £20 million from the Government's Levelling Up Fund, focuses on revitalising Ashton Market Square and the Outdoor Market to transform the town centre, create job opportunities, and provide improved public spaces with better stalls, paving, and pedestrian-friendly areas.
projects.justification: Construction began 2024, physical works verifiably underway with kiosks installed and trees planted, on track for Spring 2026 completion.

citations.finding: Planning permission granted September 2023, main construction works began in 2024, continuing through March 2026.
First new kiosks now on site, transformation making strong progress, on track to reopen Spring 2026.
Trees have arrived in Ashton Market Square, making strong progress, on track to reopen Spring 2026.
Work well underway on former Ashton Market Square site as of April 2025, due to complete March 2026.

projects.project_name: The Redevelopment of Partington Sports Village
projects.summary: Trafford Council secured £18.3 million from the Government's Levelling Up Fund to refurbish and extend Partington Leisure Centre, creating an improved sports facility to address insufficient facilities and enable greater participation in sporting and leisure activities by residents and local schools.
projects.justification: Facility closed June 2024; contractor Speller Metcalfe appointed but no main construction contract signed; August 2025 tender re-issued.

citations.finding: Sports Village closed 30 June 2024 with work expected to start July 2024.
Speller Metcalfe appointed for enabling works with intent to enter main construction contract in new year.
As of August 2025, no construction firm appointed to start the job.
August 2025: construction firms invited to submit bids to complete the project.

projects.summary: The Haigh Hall project will restore the Grade II* listed building and its 250-acre woodland park in Wigan, transforming it into a cultural destination of national significance with gallery spaces, event facilities, education suite, and rooftop bar and café.
projects.justification: Exterior works completed summer 2025; planning approved April 2026; interior work scheduled to commence summer 2026.

citations.finding: External fabric repairs completed June 2025 after contractors began work April 2023.
Exterior works completed summer 2025; interior restoration expected complete 2028.
Planning permission and Listed Building Consent secured April 2026.
Planning approved April 2026; interior work to begin summer 2026.

projects.summary: The Blackburn Growth Axis Transport Package (Southeast) will widen the B6232 and A6077 to accommodate additional traffic entering the M65 at Junction 5, and create a new walking and cycling network to improve access to local amenities and tackle congestion.
projects.justification: Construction commenced January 2026 on M65 Junction 5 works; walking/cycling routes progressing with 2025 completion targets.

citations.finding: Main construction works commenced 12 January 2026, expected substantially complete early 2028.
Balfour Beatty contractor starting on site early 2026 for Junction 5 enhancement.
Work already underway upgrading junction; overnight closures starting May 2026 for next phase.
Six walking/cycling routes on track with completion dates September-December 2025.

projects.summary: The Multiversity project will build a new carbon-neutral education campus in Blackpool's Talbot Gateway to replace the ageing Blackpool and Fylde College with state-of-the-art facilities, accommodating over 2,000 students to meet employer needs.
projects.justification: Demolition work verifiably started September 2025; construction preparation underway as of December 2025.

citations.finding: Demolition started on homes in Charles Street in September 2025 for the Multiversity project.
Construction preparation underway on the Multiversity campus as of December 18, 2025.
Morgan Sindall Construction commenced phased demolition on the three-acre site off Cookson Street.
Demolition and clearance announced to take place in phases over nine months starting July 2025.

projects.project_name: Burnley Campus Expansion;  Turf Public Realm Transformation; Railway Station Accessibility Improvements (package)
projects.summary: The £19.9 million project comprises three schemes: expanding the University of Central Lancashire campus through redevelopment of former Newtown Mill, environmental improvements linking Turf Moor football ground to the town centre, and accessibility upgrades including passenger lifts at Manchester Road railway station.
projects.justification: Town 2 Turf officially opened August 2024; Newtown Mill nearing completion October 2024 for January student use.

citations.finding: Town2Turf officially opened August 8, 2024 with ribbon-cutting by Mayor of Burnley
£6m Town 2 Turf road redevelopment project finally complete as of August 2024
Newtown Mill students expected to use facilities by January 2025, nearing completion October 2024
£15m Newtown Mill redevelopment nears completion as of October 18, 2024

projects.project_name: The Accrington Acre: Our Heritage-Led Town Centre
projects.summary: The Accrington Acre project will refurbish and transform Accrington Market Hall into a food and drink destination, and renovate Burton's Chambers and Market Chambers, creating a heritage-led hub for shopping, food, events and culture in the town centre.
projects.justification: Market Hall construction underway but reopening slipped from April 2025 to late summer 2025, then to November 2026.

citations.finding: Construction work on Market Hall redevelopment continues to progress as of November 2024.
Market Hall reopening slipped from Spring 2025 to Quarter Three/Four 2025/26 as of March 2025.
Market Hall now scheduled to reopen mid-November 2026 following construction completion, as of January 2026.
First phase of Town Square regeneration completed by Morgan Sindall in August 2025.

projects.project_name: Levelling Up East Lancashire: Creating opportunities through greener, safer and healthier travel
projects.summary: The project will deliver improvements across Burnley, Hyndburn, Pendle and Rossendale through safer, greener and healthier streets initiatives and accessible, vibrant town centres, aiming to improve travel opportunities and access to jobs and services.
projects.justification: Construction expected September 2024 but tender states no contract until funding confirmed; work now planned for later 2025.

citations.finding: Construction work was expected to start in September 2024.
No contractual commitment until final approval confirmed; tender issued January 2025.
Work will start later in 2025 subject to government confirmation.

projects.summary: Eden Project North will transform a derelict site on Morecambe's seafront into a world-class cultural and tourism visitor attraction, with indoor and outdoor facilities expected to draw up to 740,000 visitors annually.
projects.justification: Site investigation began September 2025, but project missed 2024 construction start; main construction now scheduled June 2026.

citations.finding: Project achieved consent in 2022 but progressed little and missed its 2024 construction start.
Digger and machinery arrived September 1, 2025 for site investigation work to begin.
Construction will begin on 24th June 2026, with planned opening in late 2028.
Eden Project Morecambe set to open by winter 2028, with building shell up by mid-2027.

projects.summary: The £6.5 million project will refurbish three cultural venues in Colne town centre—the Muni Theatre, Pendle Hippodrome, and the Little Theatre—making them fully accessible and fit for purpose to increase community engagement in arts, culture, and heritage.
projects.justification: Colne Market Hall reopened May 1, 2026 after construction began January 2024; theatre renovations completed June 2024.

citations.finding: Planning approved late 2023, contractors began work January 2024, temporary market opened January 2025.
Market Hall set to reopen with transformed market opening Friday 1 May.
Official opening occurred Friday 1 May 2026, market now open Wednesday-Sunday.
Extended theatre due to be complete June 2024 as part of Heritage Quarter.

projects.project_name: Active Preston: Transforming Our Community Infrastructure
projects.summary: The Active Preston project aims to transform community infrastructure in Preston through a £20 million investment focused on creating a healthier, more inclusive, and sustainably connected city, with improvements to transport and cultural facilities.
projects.justification: Ashton Park sports hub component scrapped July 2024 due to spiralling costs; funding reallocated within programme.

citations.finding: City council scrapped Ashton Park Sports Hub plans in July 2024, three months after planning approval.
Ashton Park football plans scrapped as levelling up schemes branded unaffordable in July 2024.
Old Tram Bridge work underway; other schemes scaled back or dropped due to spiralling costs.

projects.summary: The Halewood Leisure and Connectivity Improvements project will deliver new and improved playing pitches at Wood Road Green Space and Halewood Leisure Centre, upgrades to other leisure facilities, and improvements to walking and cycling connectivity throughout Halewood and to employment areas.
projects.justification: Construction work commenced December 2025 on all-weather pitch upgrades; phased delivery continuing through 2026.

citations.finding: Initial work commenced December 2025 on all-weather pitch facilities upgrade; major aspects delivered in phases during 2026.
Initial work already commenced to deliver significant upgrade to all-weather pitch facilities including covered installations.
Cycling and pedestrian improvements already underway as of June 2023; projects set for completion by 2026.
Work scheduled to commence summer 2026 for coach drop-off area and other external improvements following planning approval.

projects.project_name: Liverpool City Council Docks Cultural Regeneration
projects.summary: Liverpool City Council received £20 million from the Levelling Up Fund to support cultural regeneration at Albert Dock and Canning Dock, modernising Tate Liverpool's gallery spaces and upgrading the Museum of Liverpool to boost access to arts and culture.
projects.justification: Tate Liverpool closed October 2023 for transformation, originally planned to reopen 2025, now delayed to 2027 due to funding issues.

citations.finding: Tate Liverpool closed October 2023 for transformation, originally planned to reopen 2025.
Tate Liverpool reopening delayed by two years from expected 2025 date.
Reopening date pushed back two years until 2027, announced February 2025.
Maritime Museum and International Slavery Museum closed for essential maintenance works ahead of major redevelopment.
International Slavery Museum and Maritime Museum closing early 2025 for £58m makeover work.

projects.project_name: Levelling Up for Recovery (Transport Infrastructure Improvements)
projects.summary: The Liverpool City Region Levelling Up Fund project received £37 million to create new walking and cycling routes and deliver junction improvements across the city region, aiming to improve connectivity and access to key services for residents.
projects.justification: Construction works scheduled for April 2026 on Queens Drive; £24.19m already spent by March 2025.

citations.finding: Key Route Network Levelling Up Programme construction on Queens Drive scheduled for April 2026
Key Route Network Levelling Up shows £24.19m capital expenditure to March 2025 from £49.20m total

projects.project_name: Earlestown: Regeneration through Culture, Community and Heritage
projects.summary: The project will revitalise Earlestown's historic market square and surrounding public realm, reimagine its Grade II-listed derelict Town Hall as a community and workspace hub, and improve safety and amenity at the rail station.
projects.justification: Construction underway on Town Hall restoration since 2025 and Market Square works commenced January 2026 with groundbreaking ceremony.

citations.finding: Town Hall restoration progressing following planning approval in December 2024, works underway as of August 2025.
Construction works on Market Square and High Streets began on site in January 2026.
Work well underway on Town Hall restoration with £8.8 million internal refurbishments following £1m external works.
Groundbreaking ceremony held marking construction start in January 2026 for Market Square transformation.

projects.project_name: Woodside (Woodside WaterFront Visitor and Gyratory Reconfiguration)
projects.summary: The Woodside project aims to reconfigure the Woodside Gyratory and improve green spaces and active travel infrastructure around Argyle Street, Hamilton Square, Hamilton Street, and the Birkenhead waterfront promenade, establishing a walking and cycling corridor between Hamilton Square Station and the waterfront.
projects.justification: Project underwent partial rescope and redesign in October 2025 due to overbudget cost plan; preparatory works underway February 2026.

citations.finding: Partial rescope and redesign necessary due to October 2025 cost plan being overbudget.
Council voting on value-engineered version to reduce costs and meet £25.6m budget.
Preparatory works for redesigned road layout near Woodside underway February 2026.
